content.user_title: Orchestrate Cloud Agent Swarms and Workflows
content.value_statement: Complex AI projects require coordinated agents, dependencies, queues, and monitoring. This skill guides Flow Nexus swarm creation, workflow execution, scaling, templates, and audit tracking.
actual_capabilities: Configures hierarchical, mesh, ring, and star swarm topologies through Flow Nexus MCP tools.
Spawns specialized researcher, coder, analyst, optimizer, and coordinator agents.
Creates workflows with dependencies, parallel steps, triggers, priorities, retries, and failure handling.
Executes workflows synchronously or through asynchronous message queues.
Monitors swarm status, workflow metrics, audit trails, queues, execution streams, and generated files.
Scales or destroys swarms and creates configurations from reusable templates.
limitations: Requires a Flow Nexus account, network access, and compatible CLI or MCP configuration.
Does not implement the Flow Nexus service or guarantee that documented tools remain available.
Cloud execution may expose task inputs, code, or generated files to external infrastructure.
Examples require adaptation for project permissions, budgets, error policies, and production controls.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multi-Repository Delivery
use_cases.description: Create specialized agent roles and dependency-aware workflows for synchronized development, testing, and deployment across repositories.

use_cases.title: Run Parallel Research
use_cases.description: Deploy a mesh swarm of researchers and analysts to gather evidence, compare sources, and synthesize findings.

use_cases.title: Automate Data Pipelines
use_cases.description: Model extraction, validation, transformation, enrichment, loading, retries, and scheduled execution as one monitored workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Flow Nexus swarm for [task]. Recommend a topology, strategy, agent count, and specialized roles. Explain each choice before deployment.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a clearly defined task

prompt_templates.title: Design a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Flow Nexus workflow for [process]. Define steps, dependencies, parallel work, triggers, retries, timeouts, and success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Operate and Scale a Swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the active swarm for [project]. Summarize status and workload, recommend scaling changes, identify failed work, and preserve an audit trail.

prompt_templates.title: Orchestrate a Multi-Phase Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan coordinated Flow Nexus swarms for research, implementation, testing, and deployment. Define handoffs, shared inputs, failure recovery, approvals, metrics, and cleanup.

output_examples.input: Create a research swarm for evaluating three database platforms.
output: Recommended topology: mesh, because researchers must compare evidence across platforms.
Roles: three researchers, one analyst, and one coordinator.
Execution: parallel collection followed by source validation and a comparative synthesis.

output_examples.input: Design a deployment workflow with production approval.
output: The workflow runs linting and tests in parallel before building artifacts.
Security scanning and staging smoke tests must succeed before approval.
Production deployment requires manual approval and retains rollback information.

output_examples.output: Current workload exceeds the target threshold. Add two specialized agents, monitor completion latency, and destroy excess capacity after the queue clears.

best_practices: Choose topology from task dependencies and communication needs before creating agents.
Define retries, timeouts, failure actions, approvals, and cleanup for every production workflow.
Review status, metrics, queues, and audit trails before scaling or changing active work.
anti_patterns: Do not assign every task to a large swarm without clear roles or dependency boundaries.
Do not place secrets or regulated data in cloud workflow inputs without approved controls.
Do not execute unpinned latest package versions in trusted or production environments.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It guides Flow Nexus MCP operations for swarms, agents, workflows, queues, monitoring, templates, scaling, and cleanup.

faq.question: Which swarm topologies are supported?
faq.answer: The documented options are hierarchical, mesh, ring, and star.

faq.question: Can workflows run asynchronously?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents queue-based asynchronous execution and queue status monitoring.

faq.question: Does the skill require external services?
faq.answer: Yes. Flow Nexus is cloud-based and requires network access, account setup, and compatible MCP tooling.

faq.question: Can it monitor generated files and audit history?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents execution file listing, stream status, workflow metrics, and audit trail retrieval.

faq.question: How should package installation be secured?
faq.answer: Use reviewed exact versions instead of latest, verify package integrity, and require approval before global installation or MCP startup.
